text:
maya: quick question — for the onboarding surface, should the quickstart be a dismissible toast or an inline badge with sample project cards? thinking about discoverability vs visual noise

alex: i put up two quick mocks in figma: toast (top-right persistent until dismissed) and inline badge (between header and projects grid). will share link.

phil: curious about implementation complexity — toast is easier from a placement POV, inline needs reflow and responsive tweaks. but inline might be more accessible for keyboard users.

sam: in our usability sessions users missed the toast when they were focused on the left nav. inline had higher discoverability metrics. small sample though.

maya: good call. we need to balance discoverability, accessibility, and not stealing prime real estate on the console.

alex: design notes — toast variant: compact card, 2 CTAs ("Try sample project" primary, "Dismiss" secondary), small illustration. Inline variant: full-width banner + 3 sample project cards with titles and one-line descriptions.

jen: accessibility nits from latest pass: toast uses a color that only meets AA large text, not AA normal. also no aria-live announcement when it appears. That will be bad for screen reader users.

phil: thanks — we can change palette. also can expose an aria-describedby pointing to the toast content and call focus to the first focusable element on show. but that might shift layout for keyboard users.

alex: alternative: keep toast but add a small inline anchor for keyboard/SR users (hidden visually but in DOM) so screen readers find it in the flow. adds complexity but minimal layout impact.

sam: i like that hybrid. analytics from research: users who interacted with sample projects within first session had 3x higher retention. We should maximize first-run interactions.

maya: ok decision proposal: default to inline banner on desktop (higher discovery), toast on very narrow viewports (mobile) — both variants must meet a11y: AA contrast for all text, keyboard focusable CTAs, aria-live announcement, and meaningful alt/ARIA for project thumbnails. add a hidden DOM anchor for SR keyboard users on toast.

phil: can implement. need to know copy for primary CTA — options: "Try sample project", "Create with sample", "Get started with demo" — which is preferred? also event name for analytics?

alex: copy vote: "Try sample project" is clear and action-oriented. secondary CTA could be "See sample projects" for users needing context.

sam: research favors "Try sample project" too. event: onboarding.sample_click with label project_id. also fire onboarding.banner_impression and onboarding.dismiss.

jen: QA checklist: keyboard tab order, visible focus indicator (no outline hidden), screen reader flow when banner appears, dismiss persists (local storage) and opt-out telemetry. test low-contrast mode and high-zoom (200%).

maya: i added these to the ticket. can we add an A/B test to measure clicks and subsequent retention? inline vs toast. small sample for 2 weeks.

phil: yep — i'll add flags: onboarding_quickstart_variant = inline|toast. we should also cap at 10% of new signups initially to reduce noise.

alex: quick design tweak: make inline banner's background slightly muted (not full white) so it reads as an onboarding surface but not a full modal. also ensure mobile collapses to a single stacked card.

maya: @alex can you post final figma link and copy snippets in the ticket pls. we'll schedule a short review with legal for any data collection text in the toast.

alex: link posted in ticket. copy snippets: primary CTA "Try sample project", secondary "See sample projects", dismiss "Not right now".

sam: tiny a11y nit — "Not right now" as a dismiss label is ambiguous for screen readers. maybe "Dismiss onboarding banner" as aria-label on the button. keep visible text short.

alex: good call — will add aria-label.

jen: will start test matrix once eng PR is up. also recommend screen-reader-only instruction text inside banner: "Press Enter to open sample project in a new workspace."

maya: perfect. thanks everyone. next step: eng spec + figma + A/B plan in the ticket. i'll monitor metrics and circle back in two weeks. :raised_hands:
